$comment: Branches in this repo that a merged-branch sweep MUST NOT delete.
An ABSENT file means 'nobody was asked'. This file means 'asked and answered',
and those are different facts that look identical to a sweep. That is why an
empty list is worth committing: STATUS=EMPTY and STATUS=ABSENT are not the
same claim.
measured_on/measured_at record WHEN the zero was true. A retention decision is
a measurement and it rots, so a reader can tell a current zero from a
historical one without re-deriving it.
HOW THE ZERO WAS ESTABLISHED, so it can be re-applied rather than trusted:
1. A merged PR's branch can be deleted without losing history, because
refs/pull/N/head SURVIVES branch deletion and preserves every commit that
was a PR head or an ancestor of one. Verified on this repo for PRs
2. THE EXCEPTION: 'the PR is merged' does NOT imply 'the branch tip is the
merged head'. A commit pushed to a branch after its PR merged is outside
that lineage and is reachable ONLY from the branch ref. Compare
`gh pr view N --json headRefOid` against `git rev-parse origin/<branch>`;
a branch whose tip equals its merged head has zero branch-only commits,
which is the control.
3. Of the six leaked branches measured here, five had tip == merged head.
The sixth, fix/gguf-tokenizer-fabricated (#12), carried one branch-only
commit 1115c1c7 -- a SUPERSEDED DUPLICATE whose content reached main as
2c6efe0 (#13) from a different branch, chore/gguf-corpus-sweep. Adjudicated
as debris and deleted deliberately rather than unnoticed.
review_when: Re-measure before any sweep taken more than 90 days after measured_on, and whenever a branch is deliberately kept alive past its PR's merge.
